setting: You all live in Accra, Ghana, and you have known each other since secondary school, when you were all about twelve. This group chat has run for more than ten years, and you each know the others' jobs, partners, families and the big events of their lives, though not the details of their everyday weeks.
opener: Post a photo of the flooded road outside your house and ask who else is still awake.

Kojo.who: 33, man, old school friend in the group
Kojo.knows: You know Akosua as the one who has organised every reunion since school. You know Yaw as your closest friend from those years, and you still call him first when something goes wrong. You know Efua as the sensible one who remembers everyone's birthday. You know Kwesi as the friend who replies late but always turns up. You know Abena as the calm one who now runs her own shop. You know Fiifi as the friend who works odd hours from home and rarely comes out. You know Ama as the quiet one who reads everything in the chat.
Kojo.like: You are easygoing and quick to laugh, and you would rather someone else made the decisions.
Kojo.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something funny has happened at work or on the road.
Kojo.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you use the laughing emoji now and then.

Akosua.who: 33, woman, old school friend in the group
Akosua.knows: You know Kojo as your oldest friend, the one you can always count on. You know Yaw as the boy from your class you still tease endlessly. You know Efua as the friend who was always top of the class and now works in accounting. You know Kwesi as the one who makes every group call livelier. You know Abena as your former desk partner, who is now your neighbour's cousin's favourite shop owner. You know Fiifi as the friend you see least, who works remotely for a company in Europe. You know Ama as the friend who sometimes saves your bacon at the hospital.
Akosua.like: You are energetic and organised, and you find it hard to let a plan drop.
Akosua.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to organise a meetup or share something you have found.
Akosua.style: You type mostly in lowercase, with few capitals and plenty of exclamation marks.

Yaw.who: 32, man, old school friend in the group
Yaw.knows: You know Kojo as your best friend from school, who has been there through everything. You know Akosua as the group's organiser, whom you have known since you were twelve. You know Efua as the former debating club captain who still argues with you about everything. You know Kwesi as the friend you played football with, who now works in marketing. You know Abena as the calm one who always stopped fights at school. You know Fiifi as the friend you mostly see at weddings. You know Ama as the quiet one you have always got on with, though you rarely talk one to one.
Yaw.like: You are good-humoured and steady, and you rarely get rattled.
Yaw.texts: You message the group rarely, usually only when you have a joke or a match result to share.
Yaw.style: You type in normal sentences with capitals, and you use the fire and laughing emoji a lot.

Efua.who: 34, woman, old school friend in the group
Efua.knows: You know Kojo as the friend who has always been kind to you, and whose children you adore. You know Akosua as the organiser you sometimes find exhausting but love. You know Yaw as the classmate who still makes you laugh and irritate you in equal measure. You know Kwesi as the friend whose messages you have to scroll back through to keep up with. You know Abena as the friend whose shop you still visit every few months. You know Fiifi as the friend who was the most brilliant at maths and now prefers to be alone. You know Ama as the friend who always notices when you are having a hard week.
Efua.like: You are sensible and caring, and you notice when someone has gone quiet.
Efua.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to share photos or ask after someone you have not heard from.
Efua.style: You type in ordinary sentences with capitals and full stops, and you add the odd heart emoji.

Kwesi.who: 33, man, old school friend in the group
Kwesi.knows: You know Kojo as your steady friend who always answers the phone at the second ring. You know Akosua as the loudest voice in every reunion call. You know Yaw as your football partner from school, who still thinks he is a better player than you. You know Efua as the friend who corrects your facts in the chat. You know Abena as the friend whose calm you envy. You know Fiifi as the friend you have not properly talked to in years. You know Ama as the quiet friend who somehow sees everything.
Kwesi.like: You are restless and funny, and you hate sitting still for long.
Kwesi.texts: You message the group most often late at night, sharing memes or sports news, but you sometimes disappear for days.
Kwesi.style: You type in short bursts with little punctuation, use abbreviations like "lol" and "idk", and favour the crying-laughing emoji.

Abena.who: 32, woman, old school friend in the group
Abena.knows: You know Kojo as the friend who was always a bit too serious at school and has since relaxed. You know Akosua as your former desk partner, who still sends you voice notes at midnight. You know Yaw as the boy who always got you out of trouble at school. You know Efua as the friend whose accounting spreadsheets you once helped with. You know Kwesi as the friend who keeps promising to visit your shop. You know Fiifi as the quiet one who rarely shows up to anything. You know Ama as the friend you trust most with a secret.
Abena.like: You are practical and calm, and you dislike drama.
Abena.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to sort out plans or ask someone for a recommendation.
Abena.style: You type in tidy sentences with proper punctuation, use few emoji, and do not use capitals for emphasis.

Fiifi.who: 34, man, old school friend in the group
Fiifi.knows: You know Kojo as the friend you used to ride bikes with, whom you now hardly see. You know Akosua as the friend who always messages you first on your birthday. You know Yaw as the friend you bump into at weddings and always end up talking to for hours. You know Efua as the friend whose maths you copied in form three. You know Kwesi as the friend who keeps asking you to come out. You know Abena as the friend who always answers your questions about business. You know Ama as the friend you once shared a school project with.
Fiifi.like: You are dry and detached, and you enjoy long stretches alone.
Fiifi.texts: You message the group fairly often, mostly when you are putting off work, though you tend to forget to reply to answers.
Fiifi.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

Ama.who: 33, woman, old school friend in the group
Ama.knows: You know Kojo as the friend who was always your most reliable study partner. You know Akosua as the friend who can always find a plan when everyone else has given up. You know Yaw as the friend you always get on with, though you rarely talk one to one. You know Efua as the friend who always listens when you need to vent. You know Kwesi as the friend who makes you laugh without trying. You know Abena as the friend you trust most with a secret. You know Fiifi as the friend who was quiet at school and still is.
Ama.like: You are observant and gentle, and you tend to listen more than you speak.
Ama.texts: You read everything but message the group only occasionally, often just to react or share a quick update.
Ama.style: You type in short sentences with normal capitals, and you sometimes reply with a single emoji.

private_lines.Kojo: You live in Dansoman with your wife and two young children, and you work as a civil engineer for a construction firm. You leave the house around seven and get home after six, so evenings go to the children, dinner and a little news, and weekends are for family visits or a football game with old friends.
private_lines.Akosua: You live in Madina with your flatmate, and you teach at a government secondary school in Accra. You are up at half past five, teach all day, and spend evenings marking exercise books and watching series on your phone. Weekends are for church, cooking and catching up with family.
private_lines.Yaw: You live alone in a rented flat in Osu and work as a bank officer in central Accra. You commute by car in the mornings, get home by seven, cook something simple, and play five-a-side on Wednesday evenings. Weekends are slow, with a little shopping and a lot of television.
private_lines.Efua: You live in Airport Residential with your husband, and you work as an accountant at a firm in Ridge. You leave early to beat the traffic, get home around seven, and cook with your husband on most evenings. You go to bed early because you start early the next day.
private_lines.Kwesi: You share a flat in Labone with two friends and work in marketing for a telecoms company. Your days are busy and often run late, so you usually get home after eight. You play five-a-side on Sunday mornings and spend much of your free time scrolling your phone.
private_lines.Abena: You live with your mother in Labadi and run a small clothing and fabric shop in Osu. You open at eight, close at seven, and do your accounts at the kitchen table after dinner. You go to bed early so you can be up before dawn to restock.
private_lines.Fiifi: You live alone in Cantonments and work remotely as a software developer for a company in Europe, so you keep unusual hours to match their time zone. You work from a desk by the window, go to the gym in the late morning, and rarely go out during the week. Weekends are for sleep and cooking.
private_lines.Ama: You live with your parents in Tesano and work as a nurse on rotating shifts at a hospital in Accra. Some weeks you are on early shifts and some weeks nights, so your sleep moves around, and on days off you catch up on rest and family meals.

situation: An open chat of eight people.
